name: Super Jaber
description: Jaber is a superhero in a large country that can be described as a grid with $$$n$$$ rows and $$$m$$$ columns, where every cell in that grid contains a different city. Jaber gave every city in that country a specific color between $$$1$$$ and $$$k$$$. In one second he can go from the current city to any of the cities adjacent by the side or to any city with the same color as the current city color. Jaber has to do $$$q$$$ missions. In every mission he will be in the city at row $$$r_1$$$ and column $$$c_1$$$, and he should help someone in the city at row $$$r_2$$$ and column $$$c_2$$$. Jaber wants your help to tell him the minimum possible time to go from the starting city to the finishing city for every mission.
input_specification: The first line contains three integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$1 \leq n, m \leq 1000$$$, $$$1 \leq k \leq min(40 , n \cdot m)$$$) — the number of rows, columns and colors. Each of the next $$$n$$$ lines contains $$$m$$$ integers. In the $$$i$$$-th line, the $$$j$$$-th integer is $$$a_{ij}$$$ ($$$1 \leq a_{ij} \leq k$$$), which is the color assigned to the city in the $$$i$$$-th row and $$$j$$$-th column. The next line contains one integer $$$q$$$ ($$$1 \leq q \leq 10^{5}$$$)  — the number of missions. For the next $$$q$$$ lines, every line contains four integers $$$r_1$$$, $$$c_1$$$, $$$r_2$$$, $$$c_2$$$ ($$$1 \leq r_1 , r_2 \leq n$$$, $$$1 \leq c_1 , c_2 \leq m$$$)  — the coordinates of the starting and the finishing cities of the corresponding mission. It is guaranteed that for every color between $$$1$$$ and $$$k$$$ there is at least one city of that color.
output_specification: For every mission print the minimum possible time to reach city at the cell $$$(r_2, c_2)$$$ starting from city at the cell $$$(r_1, c_1)$$$.
approach_summary: Formulate the state transition graph with non-negative weights. Execute Dijkstra's algorithm with priority queue to find shortest paths in O((V + E) log V).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1301F — Super Jaber [168. Dijkstra's Algorithm]
topic_editorial.summary: Single-source shortest path using Dijkstra's algorithm.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Because all edge weights are non-negative, the shortest distance to the unvisited vertex with the minimum tentative distance is finalized and cannot be decreased by further transitions (greedy choice property).
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Graph Modeling
Construct an adjacency list with pairs $(v, w)$ for each directed or undirected edge from $u$ to $v$ with weight $w \ge 0$.

### Step 2: Distance Table Initialization
Initialize $dist[v] = \infty$ for all vertices, with $dist[\text{source}] = 0$.
Push $(0, \text{source})$ into a min-priority queue `std::priority_queue<pair<long long, int>, vector<pair<long long, int>>, greater<>>`.

### Step 3: Relaxation Loop
While the priority queue is not empty:
1. Pop $(d, u)$. If $d > dist[u]$, discard (stale entry).
2. For each neighbor $(v, w)$ of $u$:
   If $dist[u] + w < dist[v]$:
   $$dist[v] = dist[u] + w$$
   Push $(dist[v], v)$ into the priority queue.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((V + E) \log V)$
  Every vertex is extracted from the priority queue at most once. For every edge, we perform at most one priority queue push operation taking $\mathcal{O}(\log V)$.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(V + E)$
  Required for storing the adjacency list and the distance array.
